claims.subject: e-athenian-democracy
claims.text: Around 508 BCE the Athenian politician Cleisthenes introduced reforms that set up democracy in Athens.

sources.note: Dates his reorganisation of the citizen body to about 508 BCE.
Places the election of his rival Isagoras in 508/507 and his reforms as the answer to it; the year is given as a pair.
Lists the reforms of Cleisthenes about 508 BCE as the establishment of democracy in Athens.

claims.subject: e-marathon
claims.text: In 490 BCE the Athenians and their allies defeated a Persian force at Marathon.

sources.note: Places the battle on the plain of Marathon in September 490 BCE, against the army of Darius I.
Dates the clash between a Persian invasion force and an Athenian army to 490 BCE.
Says the Athenians and their allies defeated the Persian army at Marathon in 490 BC.

claims.subject: e-thermopylae
claims.text: A Greek force led by the Spartan king Leonidas fought the invading Persian army at the pass of Thermopylae in 480 BCE.

sources.note: Places the best-known battle at Thermopylae in August 480 BCE.
Dates the famous Spartan defeat by the Persians at Thermopylae to 480.
Says the Persian army met a small Greek band under Leonidas at Thermopylae in August 480 BCE.

claims.subject: e-salamis
claims.text: The Greek fleet defeated the Persian navy in the strait of Salamis in September 480 BCE.

sources.note: Places the naval battle in the Saronic Gulf in September 480 BCE.
Gives 29 September 480 for the naval battle, a Greek victory over the Persian navy.
Says the combined Greek fleet gathered at Salamis in September 480 BCE.

claims.subject: e-parthenon
claims.text: Construction of the Parthenon on the Acropolis of Athens began in 447 BCE.

sources.note: Says the temple was built between 447 and 432 BCE.
Says the construction of the temple lasted from 447 to 438 BC; the carved pediments were finished in 432.
Says the building of the Parthenon, led under Pericles, began in 447 BCE.

claims.subject: e-socrates-trial
claims.text: Socrates was tried and put to death in Athens in 399 BCE.

sources.note: Says that in 399 BCE Socrates was charged with impiety and that his accusers sought the death penalty.
Places the trial and execution of Socrates in the spring and summer of 399.
Gives his life dates as 469 to 399 BCE; its article covers the trial and the death.

claims.subject: e-alexander-dies
claims.text: Alexander the Great died in Babylon in June 323 BCE.

sources.note: Gives 10 or 11 June 323 BCE for his death.
Says he fell ill at the end of May and died on 11 June.
Gives 10 June 323 BCE for his death in Babylon.
